results.content: A majority of US registered voters have described President Donald Trump as “corrupt”, “dangerous” and "out-of-touch", according to a new Economist/YouGov poll.The poll, conducted from September 11-14 among 1,461 registered voters, found that 53% used “corrupt” to describe Trump, while 51% chose “dangerous”. The survey had a margin of error of 3.3%.Other descriptions selected by voters included “out-of-touch” at 47%, “cruel” at 46%, and “bold” at 45%. Only 37% described Trump as “strong”, while [...] government and was saving taxpayers billions of dollars.The poll comes against a wider backdrop of concern over corruption in the US government. results.content:
Image 2: This is a horizontal bar chart showing how 1,461 U.S. registered voters described President Trump in a Sept. 11–14, 2026, Economist/YouGov poll. The most commonly selected descriptions were “corrupt” (53%) and “dangerous” (51%), followed by “out-of-touch” (47%), “cruel” (46%), and “bold” and “racist” (45% each). Fewer voters described Trump as “strong” (37%), “intelligent” (35%), “effective” (33%), “honest” (23%), “inspiring” (19%), or “steady” (18%). As a result, voters are taking Trump’s word with a grain of salt. An Economist and YouGov poll from September found that only 21% of registered voters think Trump would “definitely or probably would” issue that $5,000 dividend if Republicans retain control of Congress, while more than half (57%) said he probably or definitely would not. Even among Republicans, less than half (45%) think Trump will follow through.

results.content: Perhaps most importantly, polls are showing Trump losing ground steadily among swing-voter groups that helped him return to the White House in 2024. Economist-YouGov shows 22 percent of 2024 Trump voters now disapproving of his job performance. His approval ratio among Hispanics is 31 percent positive and 68 percent negative; among under-30 voters, it’s 26 percent positive and 71 percent negative; and among self-identified independents, it’s an incredibly low 23 percent positive and 72 percent [...] Trump’s job-performance ratings in the Silver Bulletin averages are at 38.0 percent approval and 59.5 percent disapproval, for a net approval ratio of minus-21.6 percent, a new second-term low. Opinions on Trump Closely Align With Vote Intentions Across North Carolina Contests

Views of President Donald Trump are strongly associated with how North Carolina voters say they intend to vote across the 2026 ballot. Among voters who approve of Trump’s job performance, roughly seven in 10 say they would vote for the Republican candidate in the U.S. Senate race, the U.S. House, North Carolina House, and state Senate generic ballots, and the North Carolina Supreme Court contest.
